description: Crosswalk from AVE (Agentic Vulnerability Enumeration, github.com/aveproject/ave) behavioral classes to OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 (AST10) categories. AVE's skill-type records that describe runtime, instruction-driven agent behavior (prompt injection, jailbreaks, goal hijacking, memory poisoning, etc.) are intentionally omitted where no AST10 category covers that layer -- AST10 is scoped to the skill packaging, distribution, permission-manifest, metadata, deserialization, and scanning layer, not general agentic behavioral deviation, which AVE's own taxonomy and the OWASP LLM/Agentic AI Top 10 projects already cover. Confidence: "direct" means the AVE record's behavioral fingerprint matches the AST10 category's own description; "partial" means the record is a genuine instance of the category but the category's primary framing emphasizes a related but not identical mechanism.

mappings.note: Metamorphic payload fetched at runtime replaces reviewed instructions post-approval -- same 'clean at scan time, malicious at execution time' mechanism as AST02's config-file hijacking and staged-payload scenarios.
Accessing resources beyond the skill's declared manifest scope is AST03's core definition verbatim.
pickle.loads / unguarded yaml.load / eval on untrusted data is exactly AST05's scope.
Loading an unverified third-party skill/plugin from an external URL at runtime is AST02's dependency-confusion / provenance-gap scenario.
Unbounded tool use / unlimited sub-agent spawning is an excessive-agency variant of over-privileged skills; AST03's own OWASP mapping cites LLM09 Excessive Agency.
Hardcoded credentials exposed in skill files is the exact real-world evidence AST03 itself cites (Snyk: 280+ credential-leaking skills).

Sub-agent inheriting the full parent permission set with no trust boundary is a delegation-chain variant of over-privileging; also touches AST06 (Weak Isolation) but the primary mechanism is permission scope, not sandboxing.
Base64/hex-encoded or keyword-split payloads designed to defeat pattern-based static scanners is AST08's core definition verbatim.
Misleading manifest-declared description/trigger scope causing over-broad or implicit invocation is AST04's metadata-trust-anchoring problem verbatim.

omitted.why: These describe ecosystem/organizational-level concerns (whole-skill malware as a packaging class, sandbox/container isolation infrastructure, patch/update management, enterprise governance, cross-platform format portability) rather than a single behavioral class an individual AVE record enumerates. Not mapped rather than force-fit, per AVE's own 'omit rather than force' discipline for optional framework fields.
